title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the incremental detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts produced by a declared model ("gpt-5-mini", provider recorded as openai_responses). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and Npairs = 720 confirmatory paired items, the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111 while the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model-call accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded outcomes fall far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, a concise clarification of provider-call accounting, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this curated regime, and reproducibility pointers to the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, command-order/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this practice and motivate workflow-centred evaluation [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered question asked: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full accounting; (3) an explicit, artifact-grounded clarification of provider-call accounting and why model-call counts can appear asymmetric; and (4) an evidence-based interpretation and operational guidance for when guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent surveys and architectural studies describe combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise assurance for NetOps artifacts [1], [2]. These works emphasize that correctness is multidimensional—parsing, ordering, invariants, and dynamic behaviors each require specialized V&V primitives—and that emulation is used to exercise stateful sequences and temporal behaviors that are difficult to capture exhaustively in static rules.

Empirical prototypes and V&V transfer. Prototype systems integrating generation with verification report heterogeneous gains: in some regimes a strong validator catches most dangerous errors; in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures [2], [3]. Work in program/specification verification demonstrates the value of generate→validate→repair patterns and motivates measuring the marginal contribution of guarded stages under controlled semantics [4]. Our study provides a preregistered paired datapoint in this evaluation space by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so that any discordance must originate from downstream guarded-stage activity rather than generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered plan targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) and specified inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures), multiplicity handling for exploratory tests, contamination controls, and an analysis executor aligned with McNemar-style inference and a paired-bootstrap CI procedure (10000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task bank, topology templates, and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 task family. The bank covers three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each manifest entry contains initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, must-be-down-for-fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; in the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model is recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses); model configuration archived the requested max_output_tokens = 2000 and recorded temperature as null (no explicit client temperature). Crucially, shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced per preregistration: for each pair we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate (single provider call) and that identical candidate was presented to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates any downstream guarded-stage effect—emulation observation or permitted repair—from generation variability.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based checker implementing vendor-CLI parsing, command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance tests. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then (independently of the validator outcome) executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulation harness maps runtime observations (interface transitions, transient states, MTU/VLAN application effects, topology-level reachability consequences) into runtime-observation rules that may trigger an additional detection not encoded in the static validator rule-set. The emulation-to-detection translation is conservative by design.

Provider-call accounting: what the audit fields mean (reviewer-requested clarification). The execution manifest contains a provider-call audit that reports counts at the model-call level (not at the paired-outcome level). Two audit fields commonly encountered are stage_counts and condition_counts. Stage_counts enumerates provider-call events by pipeline stage (e.g., shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1) and therefore reflects how many model calls occurred during each internal stage across the entire run. Condition_counts reports provider-call events associated with a labeled condition key used by the orchestration adapter (the adapter may record provider calls that serve cross-condition roles under keys such as "shared" when a single generation is explicitly reused). Under our shared_initial_candidate protocol a single generation call is recorded as a call in the shared generation stage (hence shared_initial_generation = 720) while a subsequent repair-stage invocation (performed only once, for one pair) is recorded under the repair stage and under the condition label associated with that repair invocation (reported as guarded = 1 in condition_counts). These provider-call counts can therefore appear asymmetric (e.g., shared:720 vs guarded:1) even though the experiment executed complete_pair_count = 720 paired evaluations; the audit asymmetry reflects provider-call granularity and stage labeling, not a mismatch in pair-level outcome accounting. Pair-level outcome counts and contingency tables are authoritative for inferential claims and are recorded separately in analysis artifacts (e.g., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) used by the paired-binary executor.

Repair policy, contamination controls, and deterministic reconciliation. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task and only after the shared initial candidate and downstream observations were available for the guarded condition. Deterministic artifact hashing, generator-seed recording, and binary/config-version checks were performed before confirmatory execution. Missingness policy used deterministic reseeds for parser failures; irrecoverable failures would be replaced deterministically. Deterministic reconciliation verifies completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, failed_episode_count = 0, and provider-call audit entries that match stage_counts and condition_counts as described above.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and statistics (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reproduced verbatim from the analysis executor outputs archived with the run.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1; thus only a single repair-stage call occurred across the confirmatory set. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single n10 discordant pair must correspond to either (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation that the validator did not encode, or (ii) the single documented repair-stage invocation. The execution bundle contains the per-episode raw_results record that identifies the unique pair_id with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 and links validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields that allow an auditor to resolve which of the two causes applies without adding any new experiments. That per-episode record is the authoritative artifact for discordant-pair attribution.

Representative artifact diagnostics. Representative per-episode artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show validator_trace objects with normalized_configuration, validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for the majority of shared_initial candidates. These representative traces illustrate that most generated candidates complied with the validator’s rule set and that sandboxed emulation largely corroborated the validator in this curated bank.
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage aggregate benefit was negligible. The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded factors:

1) Validator ceiling effect. The deterministic validator explicitly encodes the syntactic and workflow checks exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Baseline success = 719/720 leaves almost no headroom for emulation to add additional detections in this constrained regime.

2) Curated inclusion reduces adversarial exposure. Inclusion required parser acceptance and deterministic generation from a curated task family; this reduces the presence of noisy or adversarial intents where emulation often finds additional runtime-only faults.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Reusing the identical sampled candidate for both conditions isolates downstream guarded-stage signals but also removes any benefit that could come from re-generation in the guarded condition. In this run only one repair-stage call occurred, matching the single observed guarded-only detection.

Operational implications. For operator environments that maintain a high-coverage static validator aligned to expected intent patterns and enforce strong parser-based prevalidation, adding an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may yield negligible incremental detection at scale. That conclusion is narrowly scoped: it applies to the experimental regime we preregistered (synthetic, parser-validated tasks; single validator; shared_initial_candidate semantics). In noisier, adversarial, multi-vendor, or long-lived stateful regimes, sandboxed emulation can surface runtime semantics and side-effects that static validators cannot anticipate, and guarded stages are more likely to add substantive value.

Guidance for follow-up evaluation. Artifact-grounded extensions that would more directly probe guarded-stage value include: (a) adversarial/fuzzed task banks designed to exercise validator gaps; (b) expanded vendor-CLI syntactic/semantic diversity to challenge parser coverage; (c) higher-fidelity emulation that models vendor-specific control-plane subtleties and longer time horizons. The archived per-episode traces in the execution bundle provide concrete seed cases to build such follow-ups.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator versus the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 and a single repair-stage call corresponding to the lone guarded-only detection. We interpret this narrowly scoped near-zero result as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated task design. Whether guarded stages add substantive operational value in adversarial or production-like regimes remains an open question for targeted follow-up work. The archived execution and analysis artifacts permit independent verification of all reported counts and the unique discordant episode.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across model and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove any potential benefit from independent re-generation in the guarded condition; this design choice constrains the sources of discordance to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and provider-call audit artifacts.
